# Habitat Web Map

An interactive map, made in Javascript, to explore ecological datasets relating to habitats and conservation.

The app is built using React, Vite, and Tailwind.

## Project file structure

* `eslint.config.js`: Configuration file for ESLint, which does linting (code syntax checking) for Javascript. Linting isn’t run automatically but you can run it with `npx eslint src`.
* `index.html`: The HTML ‘entry point’. Vite takes this file and injects the Javascript through the `root` div.
* `package-lock.json`: A file auto-generated by `npm`, it records exact versions of packages used, to allow reproducibility.
* `package.json`: Contains the project metadata and dependencies. This allows the project to be managed with `npm`.
* `postcss.config.js`: Configuration for PostCSS. Shouldn’t need many changes.
* `public/`: For storing static assets (such as text or images) that are intended to be served directly instead of bundled. Typically this will include: favicons, robots.txt, large files, and files that need public URLs.
* `README.md`: This file, gives a description of the project and instructions on how to use it.
* `src/`: Appplication source code (such as the main app and CSS styling).
	* `App.jsx`: The app itself.
	* `assets/`: Assets (such as text or images) that are intended to be bundled by Vite, in other words inserted into the web pages.
	* `index.css`: Loads global styles (formatting).
	* `main.jsx `: This is the ‘entry point’ for the React app. It injects the app into the main HTML page as well as importing CSS.
* `tailwind.config.js`: Configuration for Tailwind. Rarely changed but can be used to set how Tailwind scans files to apply CSS.
* `vite.config.js`: Configuration for Vite. Shouldn’t need many changes, but for example it defines the base path used during deployment.

Files not included in the repo, but generated when building the pages:

* `dist/`: Contains built output of the code.
* `node_modules/`: Contains all the Javascript modules used in the app, installed using Node.js.

## Project styling (CSS)

The styling (formatting) is handled using Tailwind. For example, in the elements

```html
<div className="p-6">
	<h2 className="text-xl font-bold mb-4">Menu</h2>
	<p className="text-gray-600">Sidebar content here</p>
</div>
```

the `className` classes are pre-defined by Tailwind and control the formatting of the elements.

## Other notes

### What are `.jsx` files?

JavaScript XML (JSX) files are commonly used when writing Javascript with the React library. It allows HTML markup to be used directly in Javascript, like:

```
const element = <h1>Hello, world!</h1>;
```
The files have to be transpiled (converted to regular Javascript) before a browser can understand them.
